Deux pièces sous les toits, rue de l'Uni:
Two rooms under the roof, Unity Street. Vera SEDLAR opens the door in her schoolteacher's smock, a red exercise book in her hand. The child sits on his bed and says nothing.

"Do what you have to do."

You have time to search four places, in either room.
Sous des nappes repassées, une ordonnanc: Under ironed tablecloths, a prescription from Halvek-South hospital in the name of Irena SEDLAR: a heart treatment that cannot be found in Velmira. The paper has been folded and unfolded many times.
Dans les cendres froides, un papier à mo: In the cold ashes, a half-burnt paper. You can make out a hand-drawn clock with no hands, and the time "06h05". You have seen that drawing before, scratched into your stairwell.
Une photo de 1979 : SEDLAR, Vera, une vi: A photo from 1979: SEDLAR, Vera, an old woman in front of a house in Halvek. On the back, in pencil: "ORLIK, Saturday, the boiler". Vera looks away.
Des cahiers d'élèves, corrigés à l'encre: Pupils' exercise books, corrected in red ink. Nothing else. Vera watches you leaf through her eight-year-olds' dictations without a word. She will not forget.
Une enveloppe : un formulaire de demande: An envelope: an application form for medical treatment abroad, filled in with careful handwriting. The doctor's signature was first traced in pencil, then gone over in ink. It is a forgery, and a clumsy one.
L'enfant se lève pour vous laisser la pl: The child gets up to make room for you. Under the pillow, a drawing: a train, a house, a little figure waving. Written underneath: "daddy on the train".
Vera referme la porte derrière vous sans: Vera closes the door behind you without slamming it. On the landing opposite, a spyhole goes dark.
